report.summary: Fixes the input schema for list_issue_labels, the one tempo MCP tool with no arguments. Effect 4.0.3 renders a struct with no fields as {not:{type:"null"}} (see internal/schema/toJsonSchemaDocument.ts), which is not type "object" as MCP clients require. The new toolInputSchema helper returns {type:"object",properties:{},additionalProperties:false} for empty structs and leaves structs with fields unchanged. This matches decoding on tools/call (onExcessProperty: "error") and the docs/09 rule that issue-tool schemas are the API inputs with projectId removed. The new test fails on the old output and checks every listed tool, both outside a run and inside a run with a review report. Nothing blocks. I could not run typecheck or the tests because the worktree has no node_modules; I checked type assignability by reading Effect's Struct interface.

findings.text: The new helper was inserted under the existing comment for handleMcpMessage, so that comment now sits above toolInputSchema. Not blocking.

evidence.quote:
/** Handles one JSON-RPC message; returns the response, or null for a notification. */
/** MCP clients require `type: "object"`; Effect renders a struct with no fields as any non-null value. */
evidence.why: Two doc comments now stack above toolInputSchema, and handleMcpMessage has none. This affects only documentation, not behavior.

findings.text: I did not run typecheck or the tests: the worktree has no node_modules, and installing would modify it. By reading, Effect's Struct exposes fields as a readonly property and mapFields with method syntax, so Struct<F> should be assignable to Struct<Struct.Fields>. A green bun run typecheck and the tempod test suite in CI would confirm it.

evidence.why: Assignability was checked only by reading the code, not by running the compiler.

checked.risk: Real contracts: Effect 4.0.3 JSON Schema output for an empty struct, MCP tools/list inputSchema shape, and call-time decoding
Failure paths: the advertised schema against what tools/call accepts and rejects
Spec: MCP tool listing (01) and issue-tool schemas (09)
Tests: the assertion runs for every listed tool, fails on the old output, and uses no sleeps or shared state
Security, idempotency, build environment: not touched by this change
